slide_master_policy.heading: Design Once. Reuse Consistently.
slide_master_policy.coreArchitecture: Slide Master view governs master-level branding, typography inheritance, and custom layout placeholders across the entire presentation.
slide_master_policy.desktopVsWebRequirement: Full authoring and editing of custom Slide Master layouts requires the desktop edition of Microsoft PowerPoint. PowerPoint for the web supports applying existing layouts but does not provide complete custom Slide Master authoring.
commonErrors: Pasting logos manually across individual slides instead of placing on the Slide Master.
Hardcoding text box dimensions on slide bodies instead of using master placeholders.
Inconsistent margins caused by manual drag-and-drop alignment.
Font incompatibilities when non-standard fonts are used without embedding.

chart_linking_policy.heading: Keep the Information Editable—and the Numbers Accurate.

methods.nativePowerPoint: Insert Chart directly within PowerPoint, storing data in an embedded mini-worksheet. Preferred for portable, standalone decks.
methods.embeddedExcel: Copy an existing Excel chart and embed the workbook within PowerPoint. Fully editable, but caution required to prevent accidental sharing of confidential source sheets.
methods.linkedExcel: Link PowerPoint directly to an external Excel file for real-time data updates. Requires maintaining exact relative file paths; broken links occur if the source workbook is moved, renamed, or delivered without dependencies.
methods.staticImage: Pasting as a picture is reserved for fixed historical references only; core business presentations must use editable charts.

chart_linking_policy.handoverRule: When delivering presentations to clients, test all chart links and confirm whether embedded standalone data or external linked workbooks are required.

information_design_ethics.heading: A Good Chart Must Be Accurate Before It Is Attractive.
qualityChecks: Zero baseline maintained for bar and column charts to prevent visual scale exaggeration.
Explicit measurement units, currency symbols, and reporting timeframes clearly stated.
No misleading 3D effects that distort data slice perspectives.
Meaningful contrast and non-colour-only data encoding for accessibility.
Documented data source footnotes on every analytical slide.

motion_accessibility_policy.heading: Use Motion to Explain—not Distract.
principles: Transitions should be subtle and restrained (Fade or Push) with consistent duration (0.5s–0.8s).
Morph transitions provide smooth object transformation across duplicate slides where supported by Microsoft 365 or modern perpetual editions.
Animation Pane must be used to sequence complex reveals progressively, preventing cognitive overload.
Motion must never trigger photosensitive discomfort or distract from core business comprehension.
accessibilityChecklist: Unique and descriptive slide titles on every slide for screen reader navigation.
Verified reading order configured in the Selection Pane or Reading Order Pane.
High-contrast text against solid or subtle backgrounds (minimum 4.5:1 ratio).
Informative alternative text (alt text) for photos and diagrams, flagging decorative elements.
Pass PowerPoint's built-in Accessibility Checker without unresolved structural warnings.

tools_policy.primarySoftware: Microsoft PowerPoint for Microsoft 365 (Windows Desktop preferred)
supportingTools: Microsoft Excel (for chart data modeling and linked workbooks)
Canva or Adobe Photoshop (for supplementary image editing and graphic asset preparation)
Microsoft Copilot in PowerPoint (optional, where licensed, for drafting slide outlines and summaries)
tools_policy.responsibleAiRule: AI-generated slide drafts must undergo rigorous human verification: verify all numbers, eliminate fabricated factual claims, and convert generic layout outputs into custom Slide Master designs.

curriculum.practical_assignment: Create a reusable corporate PowerPoint template.
curriculum.assessment:
A reusable PowerPoint template such as `.potx`, plus a reviewable `.pptx` demonstration where appropriate.

A `.thmx` theme may be supplied as supporting evidence.

### IMPORTANT TECHNICAL DISTINCTION

A PowerPoint theme and a PowerPoint template are related but not identical.

A theme primarily specifies coordinated colours, fonts and effects.

A template can include the theme plus master layouts, placeholders and reusable structure.

Creating and saving a custom template requires suitable desktop PowerPoint functionality.

Do not claim that PowerPoint for the web provides identical Slide Master authoring capabilities.

A reusable PowerPoint template such as `.potx`, plus a reviewable `.pptx` demonstration where appropriate.

A `.thmx` theme may be supplied as supporting evidence.

### IMPORTANT TECHNICAL DISTINCTION

A PowerPoint theme and a PowerPoint template are related but not identical.

A theme primarily specifies coordinated colours, fonts and effects.

A template can include the theme plus master layouts, placeholders and reusable structure.

Creating and saving a custom template requires suitable desktop PowerPoint functionality.

Do not claim that PowerPoint for the web provides identical Slide Master authoring capabilities.

portfolio.title: Professional Presentation Design Portfolio
portfolio.objective: Develop and verify three distinct presentation design deliverables: a complete 12-slide corporate business deck, a reusable Slide Master theme/template system, and a 5-slide before/after redesign exercise, supported by editable source files and export quality checklists.
portfolio.countingRule: Three separate deliverables: 1. A 12-slide business deck, 2. A reusable PowerPoint template system (.potx/.pptx), and 3. A 5-slide before/after presentation redesign exercise.

deliverables.title: Corporate Business Presentation (12-Slide Deck)
deliverables.scenario: Create a complete, cohesive 12-slide corporate presentation based on a realistic business brief covering company overview, market problem, core solutions, process workflows, KPI results, editable chart analysis, implementation roadmap, and strategic recommendations.
suggested_slide_structure: Slide 1: Corporate Cover (Brand identity, title, subtitle, presenter metadata)
Slide 2: Executive Overview (High-level summary and meeting objectives)
Slide 3: Business Context / Problem Statement (Market challenge and pain points)
Slide 4: Target Audience / Market Landscape (Demographics and opportunity)
Slide 5: Core Product / Service Solution (Value propositions and features)
Slide 6: Process / Workflow Diagram (Visual step-by-step methodology)
Slide 7: Operational Data / KPI Summary (Card metrics and reporting period)
Slide 8: Editable Business Chart Analysis (Native PowerPoint column/bar chart)
Slide 9: Strategic Comparison Matrix (Alternatives and competitive advantages)
Slide 10: Implementation Plan / Project Timeline (Phased milestone roadmap)
Slide 11: Key Recommendations & Financial Impact (Evidence-based takeaways)
Slide 12: Closing Summary / Call to Action (Next steps and contact details)
mandatory_skills: Strict visual hierarchy and editorial headline structures
Consistent brand styling (typography pairings, palette harmony, grid layout)
Editable native PowerPoint charts (no full-slide static screenshots)
Process diagrams and infographics built with PowerPoint shapes
Slide Master layout inheritance and non-overflowing text boxes
Accessibility check and high-resolution PDF export

deliverables.title: Corporate PowerPoint Theme & Template System
deliverables.scenario: Design an institutional presentation design system built directly inside Slide Master to ensure company-wide formatting consistency.
required_components: Theme colour palette with defined primary, accent, and background tones
Theme font definitions (coordinated header and body typefaces)
Slide Master with master-level header, footer, and slide number controls
At least 5 custom slide layouts: 1. Cover, 2. Section Divider, 3. Text & Image, 4. Chart/KPI, 5. Summary/Closing
Standardized content, text, and media placeholders positioned on a consistent grid
Brief template usage instructions documenting font rules and placeholder behavior

deliverables.title: Five-Slide Before/After Presentation Redesign
deliverables.scenario: Diagnose and resolve five critical presentation design problems across five distinct poorly formatted source slides.

redesign_cases.slide_title: Poor Typography to Clear Editorial Hierarchy
redesign_cases.original_problem: Excessive font sizes, weak contrast, and unreadable wall of body text.
redesign_cases.redesign_solution: Strong action headline, consistent 2-level typographic hierarchy, and intentional line-spacing.

redesign_cases.slide_title: Cluttered Layout to Clean Focused Composition
redesign_cases.original_problem: Decorative clip-art icons, unnecessary shapes, and zero whitespace creating cognitive overload.
redesign_cases.redesign_solution: Simplified 3-column layout with ample whitespace, aligned elements, and purposeful iconography.

redesign_cases.slide_title: Misleading Chart to Honest Data Visualization
redesign_cases.original_problem: Distorted 3D pie chart with truncated axes, missing units, and unlabelled categories.
redesign_cases.redesign_solution: Clean 2D horizontal bar chart with zero baseline, clear data labels, source note, and key takeaway.

redesign_cases.slide_title: Inconsistent Branding to Harmonious Brand System
redesign_cases.original_problem: Mismatched random colors, conflicting fonts, and misaligned text boxes.
redesign_cases.redesign_solution: Applied corporate theme colors, standardized fonts, and snapped elements to a 12-column grid.

redesign_cases.slide_title: Dense Text Wall to Structured Process Infographic
redesign_cases.original_problem: Lengthy multi-paragraph description of an operational workflow.
redesign_cases.redesign_solution: Converted narrative into an editable 4-step horizontal process diagram with concise summary captions.

deliverables.deliverable_format: 10-slide comparative presentation (5 original problem slides + 5 redesigned solution slides) with concise design rationale notes.

assessment_model.completionRule: Students must submit the complete 12-slide business deck, reusable template system, and 5-slide before/after redesign exercise with editable source files. Visual decoration without underlying master-layout discipline or editable chart accuracy will not receive passing evaluation.

faq.question: What is Microsoft PowerPoint — Professional Presentation Design?
faq.answer: It is a practical PowerPoint certification focused on professional slide design, templates, editable charts, accessible presentations and business-ready file delivery.

faq.question: How long is the course?
faq.answer: Four weeks with 32 learning hours.

faq.question: What is the fee?
faq.answer: ₹4,900, subject to Nova Skills' verified pricing and tax policy.

faq.question: Is it suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. Basic computer knowledge is sufficient.

faq.question: What software will I learn?
faq.answer: Microsoft PowerPoint is the primary software.

faq.question: Will I learn visual design principles?
faq.answer: Yes, including hierarchy, typography, alignment, grids, colour and whitespace.

faq.question: What is Slide Master?
faq.answer: Slide Master controls reusable presentation layouts and consistent visual elements.

faq.question: Will I create custom PowerPoint templates?
faq.answer: Yes. The portfolio includes a reusable theme/template system.

faq.question: What is the difference between a PowerPoint theme and a template?
faq.answer: A theme defines coordinated visual styling. A template adds reusable layouts, placeholders and presentation structure.

faq.question: Will I learn professional infographics?
faq.answer: Yes, at a practical business-slide design level.

faq.question: Will I create editable diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. Students practise PowerPoint shapes, diagrams and suitable infographic layouts.

faq.question: Will I learn PowerPoint charts?
faq.answer: Yes. The course includes editable charts, tables and data presentation.

faq.question: Can I use Excel data in PowerPoint?
faq.answer: Yes. The curriculum covers embedding and linking Excel data where appropriate.

faq.question: What happens if a linked Excel file is moved?
faq.answer: The link may break and require updating or replacing its source.

faq.question: Will I learn animation?
faq.answer: Yes. The course covers suitable transitions, object animation and the Animation Pane.

faq.question: Will I learn Morph?
faq.answer: Yes, where supported by the available PowerPoint edition.

faq.question: Is Morph available in every PowerPoint version?
faq.answer: No. Feature support depends on the version and licensing.

faq.question: Will I learn Presenter View?
faq.answer: Yes. The course covers the technical use of speaker notes and Presenter View.

faq.question: Is public speaking included?
faq.answer: Only basic technical presentation operation. Speaking and audience interaction are covered more fully in Course 89.

faq.question: What is the difference between Course 89 and Course 104?
faq.answer: Course 89 focuses on presenting and communicating; Course 104 focuses on designing and producing slides.

faq.question: Will I learn accessible slide design?
faq.answer: Yes, including titles, contrast, reading order, alt text and accessibility review.

faq.question: Will I learn subtitles or captions?
faq.answer: The course introduces appropriate captioning workflows and platform-specific feature awareness.

faq.question: Will I learn PDF export?
faq.answer: Yes, including export quality checks.

faq.question: Will I receive editable files?
faq.answer: Editable PowerPoint files are required as part of the portfolio.

faq.question: Is Copilot required?
faq.answer: No. Copilot is optional and depends on licensing and availability.

faq.question: Can Canva or Photoshop be used?
faq.answer: Yes, for supporting visual assets, but PowerPoint remains the primary design tool.

faq.question: How many slides will I create?
faq.answer: The main portfolio requires a twelve-slide business deck and a separate five-slide before/after redesign exercise.

faq.question: What are the portfolio deliverables?
faq.answer: A twelve-slide business deck, a reusable PowerPoint theme/template and a five-slide redesign exercise.

faq.question: Who should enroll?
faq.answer: Office professionals, educators, students, business teams and designers who want better presentation-production skills.

faq.question: What can I study next?
faq.answer: Depending on goals, suitable next steps include Presentation Skills & Business Storytelling, Office Productivity Professional, Business Productivity Mastery or broader design programs. ---
